text: For any triangle,  (the sum of) two angles taken together in any (possible way) is less than two right-angles. Let $ABC$ be a triangle. I say that (the sum of) two angles of triangle $ABC$ taken together in any (possible way) is less than two right-angles.
For let $BC$ have been produced to $D$.
And since the angle $ACD$ is external to triangle $ABC$, it is greater than the internal and opposite angle $ABC$ [Prop.~1.16].
assertion: angle ACD is greater than the internal and opposite angle ABC

spans.label: assumption
spans.text: the angle $ACD$ is external to triangle $ABC$

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: is greater than the internal and opposite angle $ABC$

text: Let $ACB$ have been added to both.
assertion: angle ACB is added to both sides of the inequality

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: Let $ACB$ have been added to both

text: Thus, the (sum of the angles) $ACD$ and $ACB$ is greater than the  (sum of the angles) $ABC$ and $BCA$.
assertion: ACD + ACB is greater than ABC + BCA

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: the (sum of the angles) $ACD$ and $ACB$ is greater than the  (sum of the angles) $ABC$ and $BCA$

text: But, (the sum of) $ACD$ and $ACB$ is equal to two right-angles [Prop.~1.13].

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: (the sum of) $ACD$ and $ACB$ is equal to two right-angles

text: Thus, (the sum of) $ABC$ and $BCA$ is less than two right-angles.
assertion: ABC + BCA is less than two right-angles

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: (the sum of) $ABC$ and $BCA$ is less than two right-angles

text: Similarly, we can show that (the sum of) $BAC$ and $ACB$ is also less than two right-angles,
assertion: BAC + ACB is less than two right-angles

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: (the sum of) $BAC$ and $ACB$ is also less than two right-angles

text: and further (that the sum of) $CAB$ and $ABC$ (is less than two right-angles).
assertion: CAB + ABC is less than two right-angles

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: (that the sum of) $CAB$ and $ABC$ (is less than two right-angles)

text: Thus, for any triangle,  (the sum of) two angles taken together in any (possible way) is less than two right-angles. (Which is) the very thing it was required to show.
